registries.title: Death Notification to the Municipal Family-Register Office (死亡届 / shibo-todoke)
registries.authority: 市区町村役場 戸籍課 (Family Register Section of the municipal [city/ward/town/village] office) — overseen by the Ministry of Justice (法務省) Civil Affairs Bureau
registries.procedure: A statutory notifier — in priority order a cohabiting relative, a non-cohabiting relative, a cohabitant, the property owner/manager/lessor, or a guardian/curator/assistant/voluntary-guardian (戸籍法 §87) — submits the 死亡届 (death notification form), with the physician's 死亡診断書 (death certificate) or 死体検案書 (postmortem inspection certificate) attached, to the municipal office. Jurisdiction is the deceased's registered domicile (本籍地), the place of death (死亡地), or the notifier's residence (戸籍法 §88, §25). Filing this triggers entry of the death into the family register (戸籍) and resident record (住民票).
registries.deadline: Within 7 days of becoming aware of the death (within 3 months if the death occurred abroad) — 戸籍法 §86
registries.legalBasis: 戸籍法 (Family Register Act, Act No. 224 of 1947) §§86, 87, 88, 25
registries.language: Japanese (official). Forms and guidance are Japanese-only; many municipalities offer multilingual living-guides separately but the death notification itself is filed in Japanese.
registries.notes: Primary authority where a death is officially registered in Japan. shidemori (死出守, ADR-2605263800) is a community memorial substrate — NOT a state-licensed mortuary, NOT a commercial cemetery/funeral business, NOT a legal-advice service. This is an INFORMATIONAL directory of OFFICIAL death-registration/civil-registry authorities for bereavement wayfinding: it routes the bereaved to the official process; it files nothing on anyone's behalf and renders no legal or funeral-commercial service. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold. In practice the funeral director (葬儀社) often physically delivers the form, but the legal notifier remains the family/statutory party.

registries.title: Death Certificate / Postmortem Inspection Certificate (死亡診断書 / 死体検案書)
registries.authority: Attending physician (医師) for 死亡診断書; a physician/forensic examiner — and police-coordinated medical examiner (監察医) or coroner-equivalent — for 死体検案書 (unattended/unnatural deaths). Form standardized by 厚生労働省 (Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, MHLW).
registries.procedure: A licensed physician examines the deceased and issues either a 死亡診断書 (when death follows a course of attended illness) or a 死体検案書 (when the physician did not attend the final illness, or death is unnatural/unexplained — typically after police notification and inspection). The certificate forms the right half of the standardized 死亡届/死亡診断書 single sheet and MUST be attached to the death notification. Physician's duty to issue arises under the Medical Practitioners' Act.
registries.deadline: n/a (issued at/after confirmation of death; required as attachment to the 7-day death notification)
registries.legalBasis: 医師法 (Medical Practitioners' Act, Act No. 201 of 1948) §19 (duty to issue certificate); 戸籍法 §86 (attachment requirement)
registries.notes: 死亡診断書 = physician who attended the illness; 死体検案書 = examiner where no attending physician / unnatural death. accessUrl points to the MHLW vital-statistics/certificate program; the certificate is issued by an individual physician, not a single national office, hence medium confidence on the canonical URL. shidemori (死出守, ADR-2605263800) is a community memorial substrate — NOT a state-licensed mortuary, NOT a commercial cemetery/funeral business, NOT a legal-advice service. INFORMATIONAL directory of OFFICIAL authorities for bereavement wayfinding only; files nothing on anyone's behalf and renders no legal or funeral-commercial service. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold.

registries.title: Cremation / Burial Permit (火葬許可証・埋葬許可証 / kasō-kyokashō)
registries.authority: 市区町村長 (Mayor / head of the municipality) — issued by the same municipal office that accepts the death notification, under the Graveyard and Burial Act administered by 厚生労働省 (MHLW)
registries.procedure: When the death notification (死亡届) is accepted, the bereaved file a 火葬許可申請書 (cremation-permit application) at the same municipal counter; the municipality issues the 火葬許可証 (cremation permit). The permit is handed to the crematorium at the time of cremation; after cremation the crematorium endorses it, and the endorsed document functions as the 埋葬許可証 (interment permit) presented to the cemetery/grave manager at the time of inurnment (納骨).
registries.deadline: n/a for application, but cremation/burial may NOT take place until 24 hours after death (墓地埋葬法 §3); permit obtained alongside the 7-day death notification
registries.legalBasis: 墓地、埋葬等に関する法律 (Act on Graveyards and Burial, Act No. 48 of 1948) §§3, 5, 8
registries.notes: Cremation is the near-universal practice in Japan; the same permit-then-endorsement chain covers the later interment. The 24-hour minimum wait (§3) and the municipality as issuer are well established. shidemori (死出守, ADR-2605263800) is a community memorial substrate — NOT a state-licensed mortuary, NOT a commercial cemetery/funeral business, NOT a legal-advice service. registries.title: Family Register / Civil Registry Office (戸籍 / koseki — 市区町村 戸籍課)
registries.authority: 市区町村役場 戸籍課 (Family Register Section of the municipal office); national policy and supervision by 法務省 民事局 (Ministry of Justice, Civil Affairs Bureau)
registries.procedure: Japan's civil-status records are the koseki (family register) and the jūminhyō (resident record). Upon acceptance of the death notification, the municipal Family Register Section records the death in the deceased's koseki (removing them from the register) and updates the resident record. Bereaved survivors later request certified extracts — 戸籍謄本/抄本 (family-register copies) and 除籍謄本 (closed-register copy) — from this office for inheritance, pension, and account-closure procedures.
registries.deadline: n/a (records updated upon the 7-day death notification; certified copies issued on request thereafter)
registries.legalBasis: 戸籍法 (Family Register Act, Act No. 224 of 1947); 住民基本台帳法 (Basic Resident Registration Act, Act No. 81 of 1967)
registries.notes: Japan has no single national civil-registry building; the koseki system is administered locally by each municipality under MOJ supervision, so the operative office is the deceased's municipal 戸籍課. shidemori (死出守, ADR-2605263800) is a community memorial substrate — NOT a state-licensed mortuary, NOT a commercial cemetery/funeral business, NOT a legal-advice service. registries.title: State Vital Records Office (death registration) / 州人口動態記録局
registries.authority: State Vital Records / Vital Statistics office of the U.S. state where the death occurred (registration is a state, not federal, function; locally a city/county/local registrar receives the filing first)
registries.procedure: The U.S. has no national death register. The funeral director (or the person who first assumes custody of the body, e.g. a family member in most states) prepares the death certificate, obtains cause-of-death certification from the attending physician or the medical examiner/coroner, and files it with the LOCAL registrar, who forwards it to the STATE vital records office. The CDC/NCHS 'Where to Write for Vital Records' page links each state/territory office and its specific procedures.
registries.deadline: Set by each state, not federal; commonly 3-10 days after death or before disposition (e.g. Texas 10 days, Ohio/North Carolina 5 days, Pennsylvania 96 hours). Verify the specific state.
registries.legalBasis: State statutes modeled on the CDC/NCHS Model State Vital Statistics Act (a federal template, not itself law); each state enacts its own Vital Statistics Act. No single federal registration statute.
registries.language: English (state offices may offer additional languages; forms generally English)
registries.notes: Decentralized: actual authority is the state (and first the local/county registrar) where death occurred; the CDC link is the official federal directory pointer, not a registrar. shidemori is a community memorial substrate (ADR-2605263800) — NOT a state-licensed mortuary, NOT a commercial cemetery/funeral business, NOT a legal-advice service. registries.title: State Vital Records — Certified Death Certificate issuer / 死亡証明書(認証謄本)発行
registries.authority: State Vital Records office (and in many states the county/local vital records office) of the state where the death occurred
registries.procedure: Once a death is registered, certified copies of the death certificate are issued by the state vital records office (or county/city office) where the death occurred. The bereaved (typically next of kin or a person with a documented direct interest) applies in person, by mail, or online, paying a per-copy fee and providing ID. The CDC/NCHS 'Where to Write' application guidelines link each state's exact requirements and addresses.

registries.title: Burial-Transit / Disposition Permit authority / 埋火葬・遺体搬送許可
registries.authority: Local registrar / state vital records office of the place of death (the registrar who receives the death-certificate filing issues the disposition permit)
registries.procedure: Before burial, cremation, or transport of a body, a burial-transit (disposition) permit must be obtained. Once the death certificate is sufficiently complete and filed/presented, the local registrar (or state office) issues the permit authorizing final disposition and transport. The permit accompanies the body and is handed to the cemetery or crematory operator. The funeral director normally obtains it; in most states a family member/designated agent may also request it directly.
registries.deadline: State-defined and tied to disposition timing (e.g. Florida requires the burial-transit permit within 5 days after death; many states require the permit before any disposition occurs). Verify per state.
registries.legalBasis: State vital statistics / health statutes (e.g. Florida Statutes §382.006 disposition-permit provisions); modeled on the CDC/NCHS Model State Vital Statistics Act. No federal permit statute.
registries.notes: Permit terminology and the exact issuing office vary by state (some issue at the local registrar, some at county health/vital records). registries.title: Canadian Vital Statistics — provincial/territorial death registration (Canadian Vital Statistics system / Système statistique de l'état civil du Canada)
registries.authority: Provincial and territorial Vital Statistics offices / registrars (coordinated nationally via the Vital Statistics Council for Canada and Statistics Canada)
registries.procedure: There is NO federal death registry in Canada. Death registration and death-certificate issuance are a provincial/territorial responsibility. Each province/territory has a central Vital Statistics office (Office of the Registrar General, Vital Statistics Agency, or, in Quebec, the Directeur de l'etat civil) where deaths are registered, usually after a funeral director and an informant submit the medical certificate of death plus a statement/declaration of death via a local intake point. Statistics Canada compiles national death data from these provincial/territorial registrars but does not itself register deaths.
registries.deadline: n/a (set by each province/territory's Vital Statistics Act, not federally)
registries.legalBasis: Provincial/territorial Vital Statistics Acts (or equivalents); national aggregation under the Statistics Act and the Canada-provincial/territorial Vital Statistics agreement

registries.title: Ontario death registration — Office of the Registrar General (Bureau du registraire general de l'Ontario)
registries.authority: Office of the Registrar General (ServiceOntario), Government of Ontario
registries.procedure: A physician, nurse practitioner, registered nurse, or coroner completes the Medical Certificate of Death. An informant (usually a family member) and the funeral director jointly complete the Statement of Death. The funeral director (or, if no funeral provider is used, a family member taking charge of the remains) delivers both documents to the local municipal clerk's office, usually in the municipality where the death occurred; the clerk forwards them to the Office of the Registrar General, which registers the death.

registries.title: Quebec death registration — Directeur de l'etat civil (Quebec Registrar of Civil Status / Directeur de l'etat civil du Quebec)
registries.authority: Directeur de l'etat civil, Gouvernement du Quebec

The Directeur de l'etat civil then enters the death and is also the body that issues Quebec death certificates and copies of the act of death.

registries.title: Death Certificate (Certificado de Defunción) — Secretaría de Salud
registries.authority: Secretaría de Salud (SSA) — issued by attending/legally-credentialed physician on the official SSA format; forensic/legal-medical physician via the Ministerio Público when cause is unclear
registries.procedure: The physician who attended the death, the final illness, or (in their absence) any legally-credentialed physician completes the SSA-standard Certificado de Defunción after verifying death and cause. If no treating physician is available, the Jurisdicción Sanitaria of the Secretaría de Salud sends a medical-legal physician. For deaths of unclear/violent cause, the Ministerio Público is notified and a forensic physician issues it. The certificate is free, mandatory, and valid nationwide; it is the prerequisite document for civil-registry registration.
registries.deadline: n/a (no statutory filing window for the certificate itself; it is completed at/near time of death and is required before the Registro Civil will register the death)
registries.legalBasis: Ley General de Salud, arts. 388-392 (Capítulo III, Certificados); LGS arts. 346-350 Bis 7 (handling of cadavers)
registries.notes: The certificado de defunción (medical/health document) is distinct from the acta de defunción (civil-registry legal record); the certificate is presented to the Registro Civil to obtain the acta. registries.title: Death Record Registration (Acta de Defunción) — Registro Civil
registries.authority: Registro Civil (state/municipal Oficialía or Juzgado del Registro Civil; coordinated nationally via RENAPO / SEGOB)
registries.procedure: A family member (spouse, child, parent), legal representative, or person with legal interest declares the death before the local Oficial/Juez del Registro Civil, presenting the medical Certificado de Defunción plus the deceased's CURP/identity documents and declarant ID. The Registro Civil draws up the acta de defunción (the legal civil record). Initial registration is free; certified copies carry a per-copy fee (~MXN 50-180, varies by state).
registries.deadline: n/a federally — the Código Civil Federal sets no fixed 'register within N days' window; in practice registration occurs within ~24-48 hours because burial/cremation cannot proceed without the Registro Civil authorization (see burial-permit entry). Late registration (registro extemporáneo) of older/unregistered deaths is possible. (Confidence on the practical 24-48h framing: medium — driven by the burial window, not an explicit registration deadline statute.)
registries.legalBasis: Código Civil Federal, arts. 117-130 (Libro Primero, Título Cuarto, Cap. IX — De las Actas de Defunción); parallel provisions in each state's Código Civil (e.g. CC CDMX art. 117)

registries.title: Burial/Cremation Authorization (Autorización de Inhumación o Cremación) — Juez del Registro Civil
registries.authority: Juez/Oficial del Registro Civil (issues the written inhumation/cremation authorization); sanitary control of cadaver handling under Secretaría de Salud
registries.procedure: After the death is registered, the Juez del Registro Civil issues the written authorization for inhumation or cremation, having verified death via the physician's Certificado de Defunción. No burial or cremation may occur without this written authorization, and (per CCF art. 117) not until at least 24 hours after death, unless the competent authority orders otherwise.
registries.deadline: Burial/cremation: no sooner than 24 hours after death (CCF art. 117); within 48 hours after death under the General Health Law unless the competent health authority, Ministerio Público, or judicial authority authorizes otherwise
registries.legalBasis: Código Civil Federal, art. 117; Ley General de Salud, arts. 346-350 Bis 7 (Título Décimo Cuarto, Cap. V — Cadáveres)
registries.notes: The burial/cremation authorization is tied to (and follows) civil registration of the death and is issued by the same Registro Civil authority. State civil codes mirror art. 117 (e.g. Nuevo León, CDMX). The 24h-minimum / 48h-maximum window is the key statutory timing constraint families encounter. registries.title: National Civil Registry Office / Platform (Plataforma Nacional del Registro Civil) — RENAPO / SEGOB
registries.authority: Registro Nacional de Población (RENAPO), Secretaría de Gobernación (SEGOB), coordinating state Registros Civiles
registries.procedure: The Plataforma Nacional del Registro Civil is the official government portal for civil-status records. For deaths, it lets users obtain a certified digital acta de defunción online and verify the validity of digital actas, drawing on the records created by state/municipal Registros Civiles. New death registration itself is performed in person before the local Registro Civil; the portal serves copy issuance, validity checks, and CURP/related services.

registries.title: Death Registration at the Civil Registry / Inscripción de defunción en el Registro Civil
registries.authority: Registro Civil (Civil Registry), Ministerio de Justicia — Registro Civil of the place where the death occurred
registries.procedure: A death must be registered (inscripción de defunción) at the Registro Civil of the municipality where the death occurred. Registration is initiated by a declaration on the official form accompanied by the medical death certificate (certificado médico de defunción). Persons obliged to promote registration include: the management of the hospital/clinic/health facility where death occurred; the physician who certifies a death outside a health facility; relatives of the deceased or a person authorised by them; and, failing these, the director of the establishment or any resident of the house where death occurred. In practice, when death occurs in a hospital, the centre and/or the funeral home (funeraria) handles the communication to the Registry. Under the new DICIREG system, funeral homes can report non-judicial deaths certified via the Electronic Medical Death Certificate (CMDe) electronically. The Encargado (Registrar) examines the documentation and proceeds to registration.
registries.deadline: Inscription processed without delay (same day documentation is presented if no legal obstacle); the medical certificate / burial license process runs within 24 hours of death. Burial/cremation may not take place until at least 24 hours after death (art. 83). Set as: register promptly, body may not be buried/cremated before 24h post-death.
registries.legalBasis: Ley 20/2011, de 21 de julio, del Registro Civil (esp. art. 62 — inscripción de defunción; obligados a promover la inscripción); Reglamento del Registro Civil; (historically Ley de 8 de junio de 1957 del Registro Civil, art. 83 for the burial license rule)

registries.title: Medical Death Certificate / Certificado médico de defunción (CMD / CMDe)
registries.authority: Attending/certifying physician (médico colegiado); Electronic Medical Death Certificate (CMDe) issued via the official electronic system (forms historically by the Organización Médica Colegiada / Consejo General de Colegios Oficiales de Médicos)
registries.procedure: A licensed physician who has verified the death issues the certificado médico de defunción — the medical document stating the fact, date, time, place and cause of death. This medical certificate is the prerequisite document for civil registration. It is increasingly issued as an Electronic Medical Death Certificate (CMDe), activated via an Activation Code (CAC). If the cause of death cannot be certified (e.g. suspected violent or unknown-cause death), the physician does not issue the certificate; the case becomes a judicial death and is referred to the court / Instituto de Medicina Legal y Forense for autopsy.

Available types include literal, extract (ordinary, international/multilingual), and negative certificates.

registries.title: Burial / Cremation License / Licencia de enterramiento (licencia para dar sepultura o incineración)
registries.authority: Encargado del Registro Civil (Registrar) — issued by the Civil Registry; in judicial-death cases by the instructing judicial authority. Cemetery/crematorium operation and sanitary rules are additionally governed by local municipal (ayuntamiento) and autonomous-community sanitary police (policía sanitaria mortuoria) regulations.
registries.procedure: The burial/cremation license (licencia para el entierro / licencia de enterramiento) is issued by the Registrar immediately after the death is registered — no license is issued until the death has been inscribed (art. 83). The license authorises inhumation or cremation. In judicial-death cases the license is issued by the instructing court. Burial or cremation may not take place until at least 24 hours have elapsed since death. The verifications and the license must be carried out within the 24 hours following death. Cemetery admission and cremation are then handled by the municipal/contracted cemetery or crematorium under autonomous-community sanitary-mortuary regulations.
registries.deadline: Burial/cremation only after at least 24 hours from death; the inscription and license verifications are done within 24 hours following death

registries.title: Death Declaration to the Civil Registry Officer / Dichiarazione di morte all'Ufficiale dello Stato Civile
registries.authority: Ufficio dello Stato Civile of the Comune (municipality) where the death occurred — Ufficiale dello Stato Civile
registries.procedure: The death is declared (denuncia/dichiarazione di morte) to the Civil Registry Officer of the comune where the death occurred (or where the body was found, if place of death is unknown). It can be made by a relative, a person living with the deceased, their delegate or, failing that, a person informed of the death. When death occurs in a hospital or residential facility, the head of the facility transmits the notice. In practice funeral homes (onoranze funebri) usually handle the declaration on the family's behalf. The Officer then drafts the atto di morte (death act). Italy has no central/regional civil registry: each comune maintains its own registers; ANPR/ANSC is the national digitised back-end.

registries.title: Burial / Cremation Authorization / Autorizzazione al seppellimento e alla cremazione
registries.authority: Comune — Ufficiale dello Stato Civile (burial/transport authorization) and the Sindaco (Mayor) acting as health authority for cremation; mortuary police functions per DPR 285/1990
registries.procedure: After the death act is formed, the Civil Registry Officer issues the autorizzazione al seppellimento (burial permit); it cannot be issued before the mandatory observation period (periodo di osservazione, generally not before 24 hours from death). Burial may precede registration in practice, but cremation can only take place after the death has been registered.

registries.title: State/Territory Registries of Births, Deaths and Marriages (no national registry)
registries.authority: Eight state/territory Registrars (Registrars-General) of Births, Deaths and Marriages (NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, TAS, ACT, NT)
registries.procedure: Australia has no centralised national death register. Civil registration of deaths is carried out by the Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages in each of the six states and two territories. The death must be registered with the Registry in the jurisdiction where the death occurred; that jurisdiction's Registrar issues the official death certificate. In practice the funeral director lodges the registration, or a next-of-kin/executor/solicitor may do so.
registries.deadline: Varies by jurisdiction (commonly 7-14 days after disposal/funeral); see per-jurisdiction entries
